mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES at t-0w signals weaker commuting and daytime footfall, which should reduce discretionary retail visits over the next four weeks. If workplaces stay depressed while transit remains flat, RETAIL_REC should move lower relative to the prior four-week average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is higher over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES staying below -20% for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A relative improvement in TRANSIT compared with its recent floor will raise access to shopping districts and increase retail trips within one to two weeks. The effect should be visible only if transit recovers while WORKPLACES does not deteriorate further.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises at least 3 points week-on-week from a level below -40%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days after TRANSIT rises at least 3 points from below -40%.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility jumps upward, some leisure demand is absorbed outdoors instead of in shopping venues, leaving RETAIL_REC weaker over the next four weeks. This substitution should be strongest if grocery mobility is not rising at the same time.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -20% after being below -25% the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days after a PARKS rebound above -20% while GROCERY_PHARM is flat or falling.

mechanism_narrative: A combined decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES below their recent ranges indicates a tightening mobility regime that suppresses in-person shopping demand. Retail-and-recreation should weaken within four weeks because fewer commuters and fewer workplace-linked errands reach commercial areas.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -40% and WORKPLACES falls below -20% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior four-week mean after two consecutive weeks with TRANSIT below -40% and WORKPLACES below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: Higher RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects more time spent at home and fewer outside discretionary outings, which should continue to suppress retail visits over the next one to two weeks. The effect is strongest when residential time rises while transit remains deeply negative.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 6% while TRANSIT remains below -35%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 6% with TRANSIT still below -35%.

mechanism_narrative: An abrupt rise in PARKS mobility during spring weather can pull weekend leisure time away from retail districts, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. This substitution should matter most if it is not matched by a simultaneous increase in grocery and pharmacy trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though PARKS remains above -20% for most of the period and GROCERY_PHARM does not increase.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM rebounds from a small negative baseline while PARKS simultaneously normalize, routine out-of-home errands are expanding and retail spending should rise shortly afterward. The signal should show up within two weeks because these trips share the same local activity circuits as retail visits.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2% and PARKS rises above -18% in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 14 days after both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS cross the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in WORKPLACES from its late-period trough indicates easing constraints or stronger labor-market presence, and that should lift retail-and-recreation after about four weeks. The effect fails if the recovery in workplaces is only temporary and transit does not improve alongside it.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by at least 5 points from a trough below -25%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next 28 days after WORKPLACES rebounds by at least 5 points from below -25%.
